paper.title: Understanding Memory-Regret Trade-Off for Streaming Stochastic Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB in the P-pass streaming model with memory of m arms
unmapped: P passes over the stream of arms (P is a variable P_pass known to the learner); arm order may differ between passes
the learner knows the number of passes P
settings.definition_quote: In the streaming MAB problem, the $n$ arms arrive in a stream, and available arms are stored in the memory $\+M$ which has a maximum capacity of $m$ arms for some $m\le n$. The algorithm can only pull the arms stored in memory ... In this work, we consider a general setting with $P$ passes ($P\geq 1$).

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB in the P-pass streaming model with memory of m arms (lower bound)
unmapped: P passes over the stream of arms (P is a variable P_pass known to the learner)
lower bound holds even if the learner may store arbitrary extra information besides at most m arms
settings.definition_quote: It is worth noting that our \emph{lower bounds} actually apply to that less restrictive memory model. In other words, our lower bound holds even if the algorithm is allowed to store any other information, as long as it satisfies the requirement of storing at most $m$ arms.

source.label: thm:ub-general-m
source.quote: Given a stream with $n$ arms, assuming $T\geq (n+1)^2$, for arbitrary pass number $1\leq P\leq \log\log T - \log\tp{12\log\frac{n}{n-m}}$ and memory size $2\leq m< n$, there exists a $P$-pass algorithm using a memory of $m$ arms with regret R(T)\leq O(...)

results.notes: Paper's n = K, m = M_mem. Regret defined via means: pseudo-regret. Combines Theorems 9 and 14.

symbols.P_pass: number of passes over the stream

conditions: hard instances are Bernoulli arms with means 1/2 or 1/2+eps

source.label: thm:lb-regret
source.quote: Assume the parameters $P,n,m$ satisfying $1\leq P\leq \log {\log T} - \log \tp{14\log 8(n-m)}$, $T\geq n^2$ and $n> m\geq 2$. For any $P$-pass algorithm $\+A$, there exists a stochastic instance such that the expected regret of $\+A$ is \Omega(...) when $T$ is sufficiently large.

results.notes: Holds even in a less restrictive memory model allowing arbitrary extra stored information.

symbols.P_pass: number of passes over the stream

conditions: the player may remember the identities of dropped arms (simplified, strengthened model)
K = o(sqrt(T)) and K, T sufficiently large

source.quote: For any input instance, the expected regret of \Cref{algo:large-m-simple} in pass $p$ is $O\tp{2^{-P+p}n^{\frac{2-2^{P+1}}{2^{P+1}-1}}T^{\frac{2^P}{2^{P+1}-1}}}$. Furthermore, the total regret of \Cref{algo:large-m-simple} satisfies R(T)\leq O\tp{n^{\frac{2-2^{P+1}}{2^{P+1}-1}}T^{\frac{2^P}{2^{P+1}-1}}}.

results.notes: Warm-up case m=n-1 in a strengthened model (remembers dropped identities). Per-pass bound not recorded separately.

source.quote: Furthermore, the total regret of \Cref{algo:large-m} satisfies R(T)\leq O\tp{(n-m)^{1+\frac{2^{P}-2}{2^{P+1}-1}}n^{\frac{2-2^{P+1}}{2^{P+1}-1}} T^{\frac{2^P}{2^{P+1}-1}}}, when $1\leq P\leq \log\log T - \log\tp{12\log\frac{n}{n-m}}$ and $T\geq (n+1)^2$.

results.notes: Large-memory case; no iterated-log factor. Per-pass bound with factor 2^{-P+p} not recorded separately.
